items.name: flight_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: curious, natural emphasis, a hint of wonder on the route and the sunrises. Pace: fast, energetic YouTube Shorts delivery, about 190 words a minute, sentences flowing straight into each other with only tiny breaths between them; the whole Short must fit in about 40 seconds. Only ONE short comic pause, right before the final punchline line. The first two lines are the hook: punchy, stress 'west' and then 'east'. Stress the numbers. The punchline is dry and quotable. 'This is Bhoogol.' is a quick warm sign-off.
lines: From Australia, you fly west to reach Europe.
This plane flew east. Twenty-four hours, non-stop, and set the airliner world record.
The short way, past India, is about seventeen thousand kilometres.
But this jet crossed the Pacific, America and the Atlantic. Two sunsets, two sunrises.
Because records count distance. Over twenty-three thousand kilometres, more than halfway round Earth.
The record it broke? A Boeing, in two thousand and five. It went the long way too.
Controllers even offered it shortcuts. The pilots said no.
In record books, the wrong way is the right way.
